A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-life learning study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments measuring representation alignment, depth estimation, correspondence, and segmentation propagation, with additional ablations and DINOv2 results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds temporal-gap alignment results in Table 4 and Perception Test point-tracking results in Appendix C.6.

M1.justification: The CroCo architecture, masked reconstruction objective, temporal/spatial/union pairing strategies, and DINOv2 adaptation are retained. The additional evaluations do not establish any change to the proposed training or inference procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds Perception Test point tracking, extending evaluation beyond the existing depth estimation, HPatches correspondence, and DAVIS mask-propagation tasks. Training datasets and the earlier benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The existing CroCo, K400, DINOv2, and pairing-control comparisons are retained. The new point-tracking comparison uses a model trained on 850 hours of K400, a comparator already represented in Figure 7, extending that comparison to another task.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.1 evaluates temporal gaps of [17, 32] and [33, 64] frames, sampling 1,000 pairs per dataset for each 3,000-pair test set. Appendix C.6 introduces Average Jaccard evaluation on Perception Test using HD-Epic checkpoints trained on 30 minutes, 1 hour, and 3 hours. Existing experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.1 and Table 4 test CAS sensitivity to temporal gaps beyond the training range, examining whether relative alignment persists as overlap decreases. The previous pairing ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, and supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report across-life standard deviations and variability from K400 subset sampling. The added CAS table includes ± values but specifies no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, repeated-run count, significance test, or confidence-interval practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds CAS results across temporal intervals; HD-Epic scores are 0.483, 0.340, and 0.277 as gaps increase. Appendix C.6 adds tracking AJ scores of 51%, 54%, and 57% for increasing HD-Epic durations, versus 64% for 850-hour K400 training. Section 5.2 refines the alignment-onset summary from 30 minutes–1 hour to 30 minutes–2 hours. Existing numerical tables and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation, reconstruction objective, and CAS definition remain mathematically equivalent. Changes to attention-variable capitalization and TopK notation are presentational; no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, numbered contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: independently trained single-life models develop aligned geometric representations, generalize to unseen environments, and compete with size-matched diverse training data. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets preserved relative alignment at larger temporal gaps as evidence of CAS robustness. Appendix C.5 newly explains Minecraft as an edge case combining first-person 3D consistency with unrealistic visuals. The introduction also qualifies the paradigm as conceptual while discussing potential embodied-learning and personalization applications.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, identifies ALD as a GDM dataset, and newly states the existing training-pair interval of [1, 16] frames. These are documentation additions; Appendix B retains the architecture, optimization, hardware, and training-budget details. The PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: v2 adds Choi (2006) and Soska and Johnson (2008) to motivate learning geometry through infant spatial development, plus the Perception Test reference for the new evaluation. Positioning relative to CroCo, DoRA, and representation-alignment research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and terminology edits, added introductory context, clearer alignment-question wording, and a new Appendix C.1 with subsequent subsection renumbering. The main section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the temporal-interval Table 4, moves Figure 2 between columns, and changes the placement of several appendix tables. Former Tables 4–6 become Tables 5–7. Existing chart designs and qualitative image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The temporal-gap experiment makes CAS sensitivity explicit, while the point-tracking results provide additional quantitative evidence of transfer and data-duration scaling. These modestly strengthen the unchanged central claims. The tracking protocol is described mainly through a citation and its results lack uncertainty reporting, limiting the strength of the added evidence.
